<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api">GitLab REST API v19.6</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

GitLab REST API used to interact with a GitLab installation.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://gitlab.com">https://gitlab.com</a> - GitLab REST API

<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/legal/api-terms/">Terms of service</a>
License: <a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/LICENSE">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

- oAuth2 authentication.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://gitlab.com/oauth/authorize](https://gitlab.com/oauth/authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://gitlab.com/oauth/token](https://gitlab.com/oauth/token)
    - Refresh URL = [https://gitlab.com/oauth/token](https://gitlab.com/oauth/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|api|Grants complete read/write access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, the dependency proxy, and the package registry.|
|read_api|Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.|
|read_user|Grants read-only access to your profile through the /user API endpoint, which includes username, public email, and full name. Also grants access to read-only API endpoints under /users.|
|create_runner|Grants create access to the runners.|
|manage_runner|Grants access to manage the runners.|
|k8s_proxy|Grants permission to perform Kubernetes API calls using the agent for Kubernetes.|
|self_rotate|Grants permission for token to rotate itself.|
|mcp|Grants read-write access to remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for tools execution.|
|mcp_orbit|Grants access to the Orbit Knowledge Graph MCP server for graph queries and schema retrieval.|

* API Key (apiKey)
    - Parameter Name: **PRIVATE-TOKEN**, in: header.

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-access-requests">Access requests</h1>

Use this API to interact with access requests for groups and projects.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/access_requests/">External documentation</a>

## List all access requests for a group

<a id="opIdgetApiV4GroupsIdAccessRequests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/string/access_requests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/groups/{id}/access_requests`

Lists all access requests for a specified group that are viewable by the authenticated user.

<h3 id="list-all-access-requests-for-a-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "username": "admin",
  "public_email": "john@example.com",
  "name": "Administrator",
  "state": "active",
  "locked": true,
  "avatar_url": "https://gravatar.com/avatar/1",
  "avatar_path": "/user/avatar/28/The-Big-Lebowski-400-400.png",
  "custom_attributes": [
    {
      "key": "foo",
      "value": "bar"
    }
  ],
  "web_url": "https://gitlab.example.com/root",
  "requested_at": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-all-access-requests-for-a-group-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesAccessRequester](#schemaapientitiesaccessrequester)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Approve an access request

<a id="opIdputApiV4GroupsIdAccessRequestsUserIdApprove"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/string/access_requests/0/approve \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "access_level": 30
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/groups/{id}/access_requests/{user_id}/approve`

Approves an access request for a specified user in a group.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_level": 30
}
```

<h3 id="approve-an-access-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|user_id|path|integer|true|ID of the user requesting access.|
|body|body|[putApiV4GroupsIdAccessRequestsUserIdApproveRequest](#schemaputapiv4groupsidaccessrequestsuseridapproverequest)|false|none|
|» access_level|body|integer|false|Access level to grant to the approved user. For a list of values, see [roles](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/permissions/#default-roles).|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "username": "raymond_smith",
  "name": "Raymond Smith",
  "state": "active",
  "created_at": "2012-10-22T14:13:35Z",
  "access_level": "20"
}
```

<h3 id="approve-an-access-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[APIEntitiesMember](#schemaapientitiesmember)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-access-tokens">Access tokens</h1>

Use this API to interact with access tokens including:

- [Personal access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/).
- [Group access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/settings/group_access_tokens/).
- [Project access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/settings/project_access_tokens/).
- [Impersonation tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/#impersonation-tokens).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/personal_access_tokens/">External documentation</a>

## List all impersonation tokens for a user

<a id="opIdgetApiV4UsersUserIdImpersonationTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/users/0/impersonation_tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/users/{user_id}/impersonation_tokens`

Lists all impersonation tokens for a specified user. Administrators only.

<h3 id="list-all-impersonation-tokens-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer|true|ID of the user.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|
|revoked|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, only returns revoked tokens. If `false`, only returns tokens that are not revoked.|
|state|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens with the specified state.|
|created_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or before the specified time.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or after the specified time.|
|last_used_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or before the specified time.|
|last_used_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or after the specified time.|
|expires_before|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire before the specified date.|
|expires_after|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire on or after the specified date.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens that include the specified value in their name.|
|sort|query|string \| null|false|Sort results by the specified field and direction. Possible values are `created_asc`, `created_desc`, `expires_asc`, `expires_desc`, `last_used_asc`, `last_used_desc`, `name_asc`, and `name_desc`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|all|
|state|active|
|state|inactive|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": 2,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "revoked": true,
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "description": "Token to manage api",
    "scopes": [
      "api"
    ],
    "user_id": 3,
    "last_used_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
    "last_used_ips": [
      "127.0.0.1",
      "127.0.0.2",
      "127.0.0.3"
    ],
    "granular_scopes": [
      {
        "access": "personal_projects",
        "permissions": [
          "read_job"
        ],
        "project_id": 3,
        "group_id": 5
      }
    ],
    "active": true,
    "granular": true,
    "expires_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
    "impersonation": "string"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-all-impersonation-tokens-for-a-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="list-all-impersonation-tokens-for-a-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[APIEntitiesImpersonationToken](#schemaapientitiesimpersonationtoken)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Create an impersonation token

<a id="opIdpostApiV4UsersUserIdImpersonationTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/users/0/impersonation_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "expires_at": "1970-01-01",
    "scopes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "granular_scopes": [
      {
        "access": "personal_projects",
        "permissions": [
          "string"
        ],
        "project_ids": [
          0
        ],
        "group_ids": [
          0
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/users/{user_id}/impersonation_tokens`

Creates an impersonation token. These tokens are used to act on behalf of a user and can perform API calls as well as Git read and write actions. These tokens are not visible to the associated user on their profile settings page. Token values are included with the response, but cannot be retrieved later. Administrators only.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "expires_at": "1970-01-01",
  "scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "granular_scopes": [
    {
      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [
        "string"
      ],
      "project_ids": [
        0
      ],
      "group_ids": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-impersonation-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer|true|ID of the user.|
|body|body|[postApiV4UsersUserIdImpersonationTokensRequest](#schemapostapiv4usersuseridimpersonationtokensrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the impersonation token.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the impersonation token. Limited to 255 characters.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date) \| null|false|Date when the impersonation token expires. If omitted, the token does not expire, which is accepted only when [token expiry is not enforced](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/#access-token-expiration).|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|Array of approved scopes. For a list of possible values, see [access token scopes](https://docs.gitlab.com/security/tokens/access_token_scopes/). Mutually exclusive with `granular_scopes`.|
|» granular_scopes|body|[object]|false|List of granular scopes to assign. Mutually exclusive with `scopes`.|
|» » access|body|string|true|Access to configure for the granular scope.|
|» » permissions|body|[string]|true|List of permissions for the granular scope.|
|» » project_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of projects to associate with the granular scope, when access is `selected_memberships`.|
|» » group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to associate with the granular scope, when access is `selected_memberships`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|personal_projects|
|» » access|all_memberships|
|» » access|selected_memberships|
|» » access|user|
|» » access|instance|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 2,
  "name": "John Doe",
  "revoked": true,
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "description": "Token to manage api",
  "scopes": [
    "api"
  ],
  "user_id": 3,
  "last_used_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
  "last_used_ips": [
    "127.0.0.1",
    "127.0.0.2",
    "127.0.0.3"
  ],
  "granular_scopes": [
    {
      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [
        "read_job"
      ],
      "project_id": 3,
      "group_id": 5
    }
  ],
  "active": true,
  "granular": true,
  "expires_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
  "impersonation": "string",
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-impersonation-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[APIEntitiesImpersonationTokenWithToken](#schemaapientitiesimpersonationtokenwithtoken)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Create a personal access token for a user

<a id="opIdpostApiV4UsersUserIdPersonalAccessTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/users/0/personal_access_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My token",
    "description": "A token used for k8s",
    "expires_at": "2021-01-31",
    "scopes": [
      "api"
    ],
    "granular_scopes": [
      {
        "access": "personal_projects",
        "permissions": [
          "string"
        ],
        "project_ids": [
          0
        ],
        "group_ids": [
          0
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/users/{user_id}/personal_access_tokens`

Creates a personal access token for a user. To create a fine-grained personal access token, use `granular_scopes` instead of `scopes`. Token values are included with the response, but cannot be retrieved later. Administrators only.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My token",
  "description": "A token used for k8s",
  "expires_at": "2021-01-31",
  "scopes": [
    "api"
  ],
  "granular_scopes": [
    {
      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [
        "string"
      ],
      "project_ids": [
        0
      ],
      "group_ids": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-personal-access-token-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer|true|ID of the user.|
|body|body|[postApiV4UsersUserIdPersonalAccessTokensRequest](#schemapostapiv4usersuseridpersonalaccesstokensrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the access token.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the access token. Limited to 255 characters.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date) \| null|false|Expiration date of the access token in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD). If undefined, the date is set to the maximum allowable lifetime limit.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|Array of approved scopes. For a list of possible values, see [access token scopes](https://docs.gitlab.com/security/tokens/access_token_scopes/). Exactly one of `scopes`, `granular_scopes` must be provided.|
|» granular_scopes|body|[object]|false|List of granular scopes to assign. Exactly one of `scopes`, `granular_scopes` must be provided.|
|» » access|body|string|true|Access to configure for the granular scope.|
|» » permissions|body|[string]|true|List of permissions for the granular scope.|
|» » project_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of projects to associate with the granular scope, when access is `selected_memberships`.|
|» » group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to associate with the granular scope, when access is `selected_memberships`.|

|» scopes|read_user|

|» scopes|write_observability|

`POST /api/v4/user/personal_access_tokens`

```json
  "name": "My token",

  "expires_at": "2021-01-31",

      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [

      ],
      "project_ids": [

      ],
      "group_ids": [

      ]
    }
  ],
  "scopes": [
    "k8s_proxy"
  ]
}
```

|» granular_scopes|body|[object]|false|List of granular scopes to assign. Exactly one of `scopes`, `granular_scopes` must be provided.|

|» » permissions|body|[string]|true|List of permissions for the granular scope.|

|» » group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to associate with the granular scope, when access is `selected_memberships`.|


`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/service_accounts/{user_id}/personal_access_tokens`

Lists all personal access tokens for a specified project service account

<h3 id="list-all-personal-access-tokens-for-a-project-service-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|revoked|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, only returns revoked tokens. If `false`, only returns tokens that are not revoked.|
|state|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens with the specified state.|
|created_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or before the specified time.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or after the specified time.|
|last_used_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or before the specified time.|
|last_used_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or after the specified time.|
|expires_before|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire before the specified date.|
|expires_after|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire on or after the specified date.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens that include the specified value in their name.|
|sort|query|string \| null|false|Sort results by the specified field and direction. Possible values are `created_asc`, `created_desc`, `expires_asc`, `expires_desc`, `last_used_asc`, `last_used_desc`, `name_asc`, and `name_desc`.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|
|user_id|path|integer|true|ID of the service account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|state|all|
|state|active|
|state|inactive|

```json
    }
  ],
```

`POST /api/v4/groups/{id}/service_accounts/{user_id}/personal_access_tokens/{token_id}/rotate`

Rotates a specified personal access token for a group service account. This revokes the existing token and creates a token with the same name, description, and scopes.

```json
  "expires_at": "2021-01-31"
}
```

|» expires_at|body|string(date) \| null|false|Date when the access token expires. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/505671) in GitLab 17.9. If omitted, the new token expires one week after rotation when [token expiry is enforced](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/#access-token-expiration), and does not expire otherwise.|

```json
  "token": "string"
}
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/access_tokens`

Creates a project access token for a specified project. You cannot create a token with an access level greater than your account. For example, a user with the Maintainer role cannot create a project access token with the Owner role. You must use a personal access token with this endpoint. You cannot authenticate with a project access token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My token",
  "description": "A token used for k8s",
  "expires_at": "2026-02-14",
```

## Rotate a project access token

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdAccessTokensTokenIdRotate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/access_tokens/string/rotate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expires_at": "2021-01-31"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/access_tokens/{token_id}/rotate`

Rotates a project access token. This immediately revokes the previous token and creates a token. Generally, this endpoint rotates a specific project access token by authenticating with a personal access token. You can also use a project access token to rotate itself. If you attempt to use this endpoint to rotate a token that was previously revoked, any active tokens from the same token family are revoked. This feature was introduced in GitLab 16.0.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expires_at": "2021-01-31"
}
```

<h3 id="rotate-a-project-access-token-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|token_id|path|string|true|ID of the token.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdAccessTokensTokenIdRotateRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidaccesstokenstokenidrotaterequest)|false|none|
|» expires_at|body|string(date) \| null|false|Date when the access token expires. If omitted, the new token expires one week after rotation when [token expiry is enforced](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/#access-token-expiration), and does not expire otherwise.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 2,
  "name": "John Doe",
  "revoked": true,
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "description": "Token to manage api",
  "scopes": [
    "api"
  ],
  "user_id": 3,
  "last_used_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
  "last_used_ips": [
    "127.0.0.1",
    "127.0.0.2",
    "127.0.0.3"
  ],
  "granular_scopes": [
    {
      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [
        "read_job"
      ],
      "project_id": 3,
      "group_id": 5
    }
  ],
  "active": true,
  "granular": true,
  "expires_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
  "access_level": 40,
  "resource_type": "project",
  "resource_id": 1234,
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="rotate-a-project-access-token-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesResourceAccessTokenWithToken](#schemaapientitiesresourceaccesstokenwithtoken)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<a id="opIdgetApiV4GroupsIdAccessTokens"></a>

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /api/v4/groups/{id}/access_tokens`

Lists all group access tokens for a specified group.

<h3 id="list-all-group-access-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|revoked|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, only returns revoked tokens. If `false`, only returns tokens that are not revoked.|
|state|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens with the specified state.|
|created_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or before the specified time.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or after the specified time.|
|last_used_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or before the specified time.|
|last_used_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or after the specified time.|
|expires_before|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire before the specified date.|
|expires_after|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire on or after the specified date.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens that include the specified value in their name.|
|sort|query|string \| null|false|Sort results by the specified field and direction. Possible values are `created_asc`, `created_desc`, `expires_asc`, `expires_desc`, `last_used_asc`, `last_used_desc`, `name_asc`, and `name_desc`.|

## Create a group access token

<a id="opIdpostApiV4GroupsIdAccessTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/2/access_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My token",
    "description": "A token used for k8s",
    "expires_at": "2026-02-14",
    "scopes": [
      "api"
    ],
    "access_level": 40
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/groups/{id}/access_tokens`

Creates a group access token for a specified group. You cannot create a token with an access level greater than your account. For example, a user with the Maintainer role cannot create a group access token with the Owner role. You must use a personal access token with this endpoint. You cannot authenticate with a group access token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My token",
  "description": "A token used for k8s",
  "expires_at": "2026-02-14",
  "scopes": [
    "api"
  ],
  "access_level": 40
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-group-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|body|body|[postApiV4GroupsIdAccessTokensRequest](#schemapostapiv4groupsidaccesstokensrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the access token.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the access token. Limited to 255 characters.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date) \| null|false|Date when the access token expires. If omitted, the token does not expire, which is accepted only when [token expiry is not enforced](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/#access-token-expiration).|
|» scopes|body|[string]|true|List of [scopes](https://docs.gitlab.com/security/tokens/access_token_scopes/) available to the token.|
|» access_level|body|integer|false|The access level of the token in the group|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» scopes|api|
|» scopes|read_api|
|» scopes|create_runner|
|» scopes|manage_runner|

|» scopes|write_virtual_registry|

|» scopes|write_observability|
|» scopes|ai_features|

|» access_level|15|
|» access_level|20|
|» access_level|25|
|» access_level|30|
|» access_level|40|
|» access_level|50|

## List all personal access tokens

<a id="opIdgetApiV4PersonalAccessTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/personal_access_tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/personal_access_tokens`

Lists all personal access tokens accessible by the authenticated user. For administrators, returns all personal access tokens in the instance. For non-administrators, returns all of their personal access tokens.

<h3 id="list-all-personal-access-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|query|integer \| null|false|Filter personal access tokens by user ID. Non-administrators can only filter their own tokens.|
|revoked|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, only returns revoked tokens. If `false`, only returns tokens that are not revoked.|
|state|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens with the specified state.|
|created_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or before the specified time.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens created on or after the specified time.|
|last_used_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or before the specified time.|
|last_used_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return tokens last used on or after the specified time.|
|expires_before|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire before the specified date.|
|expires_after|query|string(date) \| null|false|Return tokens that expire on or after the specified date.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Return tokens that include the specified value in their name.|
|sort|query|string \| null|false|Sort results by the specified field and direction. Possible values are `created_asc`, `created_desc`, `expires_asc`, `expires_desc`, `last_used_asc`, `last_used_desc`, `name_asc`, and `name_desc`.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|all|
|state|active|
|state|inactive|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": 2,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "revoked": true,
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "description": "Token to manage api",
    "scopes": [
      "api"
    ],
    "user_id": 3,
    "last_used_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
    "last_used_ips": [
      "127.0.0.1",
      "127.0.0.2",
      "127.0.0.3"
    ],
    "granular_scopes": [
      {
        "access": "personal_projects",
        "permissions": [
          "read_job"
        ],
        "project_id": 3,
        "group_id": 5
      }
    ],
    "active": true,
    "granular": true,
    "expires_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-all-personal-access-tokens-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|

<h3 id="list-all-personal-access-tokens-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Rotate a personal access token

<a id="opIdpostApiV4PersonalAccessTokensIdRotate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/personal_access_tokens/0/rotate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expires_at": "2021-01-31"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/personal_access_tokens/{id}/rotate`

Rotates a specified personal access token. This revokes the previous token and creates a token that expires after one week. Administrators can revoke tokens for any user. Non-administrators can only revoke their own tokens.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expires_at": "2021-01-31"
}
```

<h3 id="rotate-a-personal-access-token-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the personal access token.|
|body|body|[postApiV4PersonalAccessTokensIdRotateRequest](#schemapostapiv4personalaccesstokensidrotaterequest)|false|none|
|» expires_at|body|string(date) \| null|false|Date when the access token expires. If omitted, the new token expires one week after rotation when [token expiry is enforced](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/#access-token-expiration), and does not expire otherwise.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 2,
  "name": "John Doe",
  "revoked": true,
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "description": "Token to manage api",
  "scopes": [
    "api"
  ],
  "user_id": 3,
  "last_used_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
  "last_used_ips": [
    "127.0.0.1",
    "127.0.0.2",
    "127.0.0.3"
  ],
  "granular_scopes": [
    {
      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [
        "read_job"
      ],
      "project_id": 3,
      "group_id": 5
    }
  ],
  "active": true,
  "granular": true,
  "expires_at": "2020-08-31T15:53:00.073Z",
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="rotate-a-personal-access-token-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[APIEntitiesPersonalAccessTokenWithToken](#schemaapientitiespersonalaccesstokenwithtoken)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-active-context">Active context</h1>

Use this API to administer the ActiveContext indexing infrastructure, including its connections,
collection options, the namespaces enabled for code indexing, and the dead queue.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-advanced-search-rollout">Advanced search rollout</h1>

Use this API to control what percentage of namespaces are indexed for
[advanced search](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/advanced_search/elasticsearch/), rolling
indexing forward or back.

## Rollout namespaces to be indexed up to n%

<a id="opIdputApiV4ElasticsearchIndexedNamespacesRollout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/elasticsearch_indexed_namespaces/rollout \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "percentage": 0,
    "plan": "bronze"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/elasticsearch_indexed_namespaces/rollout`

This feature was introduced in GitLab 12.7.

**DEPRECATED**: This endpoint is deprecated and for GitLab.com use only.

This will only ever increase the number of indexed namespaces. Providing a value lower than the current rolled out percentage will have no effect.

This percentage is never persisted but is used to calculate the number of new namespaces to rollout.

If the same percentage is applied again at a later time, due to possible new namespaces being created during the period, some of them will also be indexed. Therefore you may expect that setting this to 10%, then waiting a month and setting to 10% again will trigger new namespaces to be added (i.e. 10% of the number of newly created namespaces in the last month within the given plan).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "percentage": 0,
  "plan": "bronze"
}
```

<h3 id="rollout-namespaces-to-be-indexed-up-to-n-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[putApiV4ElasticsearchIndexedNamespacesRolloutRequest](#schemaputapiv4elasticsearchindexednamespacesrolloutrequest)|true|none|
|» percentage|body|integer|true|Percentage of namespaces to enable or disable Elasticsearch indexing for.|
|» plan|body|string|true|Subscription tier to rollout Elasticsearch for.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» plan|bronze|
|» plan|silver|
|» plan|premium|
|» plan|gold|
|» plan|ultimate|
|» plan|ultimate_trial|
|» plan|ultimate_trial_paid_customer|
|» plan|premium_trial|
|» plan|opensource|

<h3 id="rollout-namespaces-to-be-indexed-up-to-n-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-analytics">Analytics</h1>

product analytics data. For more information about the group metrics, see

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-applications">Applications</h1>

Use this API to manage instance-wide OAuth applications that:

- [Use GitLab as an authentication provider](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/oauth_provider/).
- [Allow access to GitLab resources on a user's behalf](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/oauth2/).

> [!note]
> You cannot use this API to manage group applications or individual user applications.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/applications/">External documentation</a>

## Create an application

<a id="opIdpostApiV4UserApplications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/user/applications \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "MyApplication",
    "redirect_uri": "https://redirect.uri",
    "scopes": "string",
    "confidential": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/user/applications`

Creates a new OAuth application for the authenticated user. This feature was introduced in GitLab 19.0

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "MyApplication",
  "redirect_uri": "https://redirect.uri",
  "scopes": "string",
  "confidential": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[postApiV4UserApplicationsRequest](#schemapostapiv4userapplicationsrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the application.|
|» redirect_uri|body|string \| null|true|Redirect URI of the application.|
|» scopes|body|string \| null|true|Scopes available to the application. Separate multiple scopes with a space.|
|» confidential|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the application can securely store client credentials, such as the client secret. Non-confidential applications (such as native mobile apps and Single Page Apps) might expose client credentials.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "application_id": "5832fc6e14300a0d962240a8144466eef4ee93ef0d218477e55f11cf12fc3737",
  "application_name": "MyApplication",
  "callback_url": "https://redirect.uri",
  "confidential": true,
  "scopes": [
    "api",
    "read_user"
  ],
  "granular_scopes": [
    {
      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [
        "read_job"
      ],
      "project_id": 3,
      "group_id": 5
    }
  ],
  "secret": "ee1dd64b6adc89cf7e2c23099301ccc2c61b441064e9324d963c46902a85ec34",
  "warnings": [
    "Tokens cannot use the MCP server without a user-level scope granting execute_mcp_tool."
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-application-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[APIEntitiesApplicationWithSecret](#schemaapientitiesapplicationwithsecret)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

```bash
          0
        ]
```

`POST /api/v4/applications`

This feature was introduced in GitLab 10.5. The granular_scopes parameter requires the granular_oauth_tokens feature flag.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "MyApplication",
  "redirect_uri": "https://redirect.uri",
  "scopes": "string",
  "confidential": true,
  "granular_scopes": [
    {
      "access": "personal_projects",
      "permissions": [
        "string"
      ],
      "project_ids": [
        0
      ],
      "group_ids": [
        0
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[postApiV4ApplicationsRequest](#schemapostapiv4applicationsrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the application.|
|» redirect_uri|body|string \| null|true|Redirect URI of the application.|
|» scopes|body|string \| null|true|Scopes available to the application. Separate multiple scopes with a space.|
|» confidential|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the application can securely store client credentials, such as the client secret. Non-confidential applications (such as native mobile apps and Single Page Apps) might expose client credentials.|
|» granular_scopes|body|[object]|false|List of granular scopes to assign.|
|» » access|body|string|true|Access to configure for the granular scope.|
|» » permissions|body|[string]|true|List of permissions for the granular scope.|
|» » project_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of projects to associate with the granular scope, when access is `selected_memberships`.|
|» » group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to associate with the granular scope, when access is `selected_memberships`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|personal_projects|
|» » access|all_memberships|
|» » access|selected_memberships|
|» » access|user|
|» » access|instance|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
```

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-approval-rules">Approval rules</h1>

Use this API to manage the [merge request approval rules](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/approvals/rules/)
defined for a project or a group, where the rules of a group apply to the projects it contains.

All endpoints require authentication. To manage the approval rules of an individual merge request,
use the [merge request approvals API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/merge_request_approvals/).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/merge_request_approvals/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="create-new-approval-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdApprovalSettingsRulesRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidapprovalsettingsrulesrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the approval rule. Limited to 1024 characters.|
|» approvals_required|body|integer \| null|true|Number of required approvals for the rule.|
|» rule_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of the approval rule. Possible values are `regular`, `report_approver`, and `any_approver`.|
|» users|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `user_ids` instead.|
|» user_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. When used with `usernames`, both lists of users are added.|
|» groups|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `group_ids` instead.|
|» group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers.|
|» usernames|body|[string]|false|Usernames of approvers. If used with `user_ids`, adds both lists of users.|
|» protected_branch_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of protected branches to scope the rule by.|
|» applies_to_all_protected_branches|body|boolean|false|If `true`, applies the rule to all protected branches and ignores the `protected_branch_ids` attribute.|
|» report_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of the report required when `rule_type` is set to `report_approver`.|
|» coverage_minimum_threshold|body|number \| null|false|Minimum code coverage percentage for the rule, from 0 to 100. If coverage falls below this threshold, approval is required.|
|» vulnerabilities_allowed|body|integer \| null|false|Number of vulnerabilities allowed for the rule.|
|» scanners|body|[string]|false|Security scanners to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» severity_levels|body|[string]|false|Security levels to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» vulnerability_states|body|[string]|false|Vulnerability states to be considered by the approval rule.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» report_type|code_coverage|

<h3 id="update-approval-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|approval_rule_id|path|integer|true|ID of the approval rule.|
|body|body|[putApiV4ProjectsIdApprovalSettingsRulesApprovalRuleIdRequest](#schemaputapiv4projectsidapprovalsettingsrulesapprovalruleidrequest)|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the approval rule. Limited to 1024 characters.|
|» approvals_required|body|integer \| null|false|Number of required approvals for the rule.|
|» users|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `user_ids` instead.|
|» user_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. When used with `usernames`, both lists of users are added.|
|» groups|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `group_ids` instead.|
|» group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers.|
|» usernames|body|[string]|false|Usernames of approvers. If used with `user_ids`, adds both lists of users.|
|» protected_branch_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of protected branches to scope the rule by.|
|» applies_to_all_protected_branches|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, applies the rule to all protected branches and ignores the `protected_branch_ids` attribute.|
|» remove_hidden_groups|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, removes hidden groups from the approval rule.|
|» coverage_minimum_threshold|body|number \| null|false|Minimum code coverage percentage for the rule, from 0 to 100. If coverage falls below this threshold, approval is required.|
|» vulnerabilities_allowed|body|integer \| null|false|Number of vulnerabilities allowed for the rule.|
|» scanners|body|[string]|false|Security scanners to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» severity_levels|body|[string]|false|Security levels to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» vulnerability_states|body|[string]|false|Vulnerability states to be considered by the approval rule.|

## List all approval rules for a group

<a id="opIdgetApiV4GroupsIdApprovalRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/string/approval_rules \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/groups/{id}/approval_rules`

Lists all approval rules and any associated details for a specified group. Restricted to group administrators. Use the `page` and `per_page` pagination parameters to restrict the list of approval rules.

|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

## Create an approval rule for a group

<a id="opIdpostApiV4GroupsIdApprovalRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/string/approval_rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "approvals_required": 0,
    "rule_type": "regular",
    "user_ids": [
      0
    ],
    "group_ids": [
      0
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/groups/{id}/approval_rules`

Creates an approval rule for a group. Restricted to group administrators. Do not use the `rule_type` field when building approval rules from the API. The field supports these rule types: - `any_approver`: A pre-configured default rule with `approvals_required` set to `0`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "approvals_required": 0,
  "rule_type": "regular",
  "user_ids": [
    0
  ],
  "group_ids": [
    0
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-approval-rule-for-a-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|body|body|[postApiV4GroupsIdApprovalRulesRequest](#schemapostapiv4groupsidapprovalrulesrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the approval rule. Limited to 1024 characters.|
|» approvals_required|body|integer \| null|true|Number of required approvals for the rule.|
|» rule_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of the approval rule.|
|» user_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers for this rule.|
|» group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers.|

```json
    ],

    ],
```

```bash
    "coverage_minimum_threshold": 0,

      "string"
    ],

      "string"
    ],

      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/approval_rules`

Creates an approval rule for a specified project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "approvals_required": 0,
  "rule_type": "regular",
  "users": [
    0
  ],
  "user_ids": [
    0
  ],
  "groups": [
    0
  ],

    0
  ],

    "string"
  ],
  "protected_branch_ids": [
    0
  ],
  "applies_to_all_protected_branches": false,
  "report_type": "code_coverage",
  "coverage_minimum_threshold": 0,
  "vulnerabilities_allowed": 0,
  "scanners": [
    "string"
  ],
  "severity_levels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "vulnerability_states": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-approval-rule-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdApprovalRulesRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidapprovalrulesrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the approval rule. Limited to 1024 characters.|
|» approvals_required|body|integer \| null|true|Number of required approvals for the rule.|
|» rule_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of the approval rule. Possible values are `regular`, `report_approver`, and `any_approver`.|
|» users|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `user_ids` instead.|
|» user_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. When used with `usernames`, both lists of users are added.|
|» groups|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `group_ids` instead.|
|» group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers.|
|» usernames|body|[string]|false|Usernames of approvers. If used with `user_ids`, adds both lists of users.|
|» protected_branch_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of protected branches to scope the rule by.|
|» applies_to_all_protected_branches|body|boolean|false|If `true`, applies the rule to all protected branches and ignores the `protected_branch_ids` attribute.|
|» report_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of the report required when `rule_type` is set to `report_approver`.|
|» coverage_minimum_threshold|body|number \| null|false|Minimum code coverage percentage for the rule, from 0 to 100. If coverage falls below this threshold, approval is required.|
|» vulnerabilities_allowed|body|integer \| null|false|Number of vulnerabilities allowed for the rule.|
|» scanners|body|[string]|false|Security scanners to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» severity_levels|body|[string]|false|Security levels to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» vulnerability_states|body|[string]|false|Vulnerability states to be considered by the approval rule.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» report_type|code_coverage|

## Update an approval rule for a project

<a id="opIdputApiV4ProjectsIdApprovalRulesApprovalRuleId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/approval_rules/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "approvals_required": 0,
    "users": [
      0
    ],
    "user_ids": [
      0
    ],
    "groups": [
      0
    ],
    "group_ids": [
      0
    ],
    "usernames": [
      "string"
    ],
    "protected_branch_ids": [
      0
    ],
    "applies_to_all_protected_branches": true,
    "remove_hidden_groups": true,
    "coverage_minimum_threshold": 0,
    "vulnerabilities_allowed": 0,
    "scanners": [
      "string"
    ],
    "severity_levels": [
      "string"
    ],
    "vulnerability_states": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/projects/{id}/approval_rules/{approval_rule_id}`

Updates a specified approval rule for a project. This endpoint removes any approvers and groups not defined in the `group_ids`, `user_ids`, or `usernames` attributes. Hidden groups (private groups the user does not have permission to view) that are not in the `users` or `groups` parameters are preserved by default. To remove them, set `remove_hidden_groups` to `true`. This ensures hidden groups are not removed unintentionally when a user updates an approval rule.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "approvals_required": 0,
  "users": [
    0
  ],
  "user_ids": [
    0
  ],
  "groups": [
    0
  ],
  "group_ids": [
    0
  ],
  "usernames": [
    "string"
  ],
  "protected_branch_ids": [
    0
  ],
  "applies_to_all_protected_branches": true,
  "remove_hidden_groups": true,
  "coverage_minimum_threshold": 0,
  "vulnerabilities_allowed": 0,
  "scanners": [
    "string"
  ],
  "severity_levels": [
    "string"
  ],
  "vulnerability_states": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-approval-rule-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|approval_rule_id|path|integer|true|ID of the approval rule.|
|body|body|[putApiV4ProjectsIdApprovalRulesApprovalRuleIdRequest](#schemaputapiv4projectsidapprovalrulesapprovalruleidrequest)|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the approval rule. Limited to 1024 characters.|
|» approvals_required|body|integer \| null|false|Number of required approvals for the rule.|
|» users|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `user_ids` instead.|
|» user_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of users to add as approvers. When used with `usernames`, both lists of users are added.|
|» groups|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers. Deprecated. Use `group_ids` instead.|
|» group_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of groups to add as approvers.|
|» usernames|body|[string]|false|Usernames of approvers. If used with `user_ids`, adds both lists of users.|
|» protected_branch_ids|body|[integer]|false|IDs of protected branches to scope the rule by.|
|» applies_to_all_protected_branches|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, applies the rule to all protected branches and ignores the `protected_branch_ids` attribute.|
|» remove_hidden_groups|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, removes hidden groups from the approval rule.|
|» coverage_minimum_threshold|body|number \| null|false|Minimum code coverage percentage for the rule, from 0 to 100. If coverage falls below this threshold, approval is required.|
|» vulnerabilities_allowed|body|integer \| null|false|Number of vulnerabilities allowed for the rule.|
|» scanners|body|[string]|false|Security scanners to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» severity_levels|body|[string]|false|Security levels to be considered by the approval rule.|
|» vulnerability_states|body|[string]|false|Vulnerability states to be considered by the approval rule.|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-attestations">Attestations</h1>

Use this API to retrieve and download [provenance attestations](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipeline_security/slsa/level_3/provenance_v1/) for a project.

> [!note]
> The availability of these endpoints is controlled by a feature flag. They are available for
> testing, but not ready for production use.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/attestations/">External documentation</a>

## List all attestations for a project

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdAttestationsSubjectDigest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/attestations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/attestations/{subject_digest}`

Lists all attestations for a specified project and artifact hash. This feature was introduced in GitLab 18.7.

<h3 id="list-all-attestations-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|subject_digest|path|string|true|Hex-encoded SHA-256 hash of the artifact.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "iid": 14,
  "created_at": "2025-09-17T02:26:10.898Z",
  "updated_at": "2025-09-17T02:26:10.898Z",
  "expire_at": "2025-09-17T02:26:10.898Z",
  "project_id": 0,
  "build_id": 0,
  "status": "success",
  "predicate_kind": "provenance",
  "predicate_type": "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1",
```

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-audit-events">Audit events</h1>

Use this API to list and retrieve the
[audit events](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/compliance/audit_events/) recorded for an instance or a group.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/audit_events/">External documentation</a>

## List all instance audit events

<a id="opIdgetApiV4AuditEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/audit_events?entity_type=Project' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/audit_events`

Lists all available instance audit events, limited to a maximum of 30 days for each query.

<h3 id="list-all-instance-audit-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|entity_type|query|string|true|Return audit events for the specified entity type.|
|entity_id|query|integer \| null|false|Return audit events for the specified entity ID. Requires the `entity_type` attribute.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return audit events created on or after the specified time.|
|created_before|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Return audit events created on or before the specified time.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|entity_type|Project|
|entity_type|User|
|entity_type|Group|
|entity_type|Gitlab::Audit::InstanceScope|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": 0,
    "author_id": 0,
    "entity_id": 0,
    "entity_type": "string",
    "event_name": "string",
    "details": {},
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
]
```

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-avatars">Avatars</h1>

Use this API to retrieve and upload avatars for [users](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/), [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/), and [projects](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/avatar/">External documentation</a>

## Upload an avatar

<a id="opIdputApiV4UserAvatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/user/avatar \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'avatar=@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /api/v4/user/avatar`

Uploads an avatar for the currently authenticated user. This feature was introduced in GitLab 17.0.

> Body parameter

```yaml
avatar: string
```

<h3 id="upload-an-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[putApiV4UserAvatarRequest](#schemaputapiv4useravatarrequest)|true|none|
|» avatar|body|string(binary) \| null|true|The avatar file (generated by Multipart middleware)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "avatar_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="upload-an-avatar-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesAvatar](#schemaapientitiesavatar)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-award-emoji">Award emoji</h1>

Use this API to manage [emoji reactions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/emoji_reactions/).

GitLab objects that accept emoji reactions are called awardables.
You can react with emoji on the following resources:

- [Epics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/epics/)
- [Issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/)
- [Merge requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/)
- [Snippets](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/snippets/)
- [Comments](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/emoji_reactions/#emoji-reactions-for-comments)

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/emoji_reactions/">External documentation</a>

## List all emoji reactions for an issue

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdIssuesIssueIidAwardEmoji"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/issues/0/award_emoji \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/issues/{issue_iid}/award_emoji`

Lists all emoji reactions for a specified issue. This endpoint can be accessed without authentication if the issue is publicly accessible.

<h3 id="list-all-emoji-reactions-for-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|issue_iid|path|integer|true|ID (`iid` for merge requests/issues/epics, `id` for snippets) of an awardable.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "lizard",
    "user": {
      "id": 1,
      "username": "admin",
      "public_email": "john@example.com",
      "name": "Administrator",
      "state": "active",
      "locked": true,
      "avatar_url": "https://gravatar.com/avatar/1",
      "avatar_path": "/user/avatar/28/The-Big-Lebowski-400-400.png",
      "custom_attributes": [
        {
          "key": "foo",
          "value": "bar"
        }
      ],
      "web_url": "https://gitlab.example.com/root"
    },
    "created_at": "2019-01-10T13:39:08Z",
    "updated_at": "2020-06-28T10:52:04Z",
    "awardable_id": 42,
    "awardable_type": "Issue",
    "url": "https://example.com/emojis/example.gif"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-all-emoji-reactions-for-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="list-all-emoji-reactions-for-an-issue-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[APIEntitiesAwardEmoji](#schemaapientitiesawardemoji)]|false|none|none|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-badges">Badges</h1>

Use this API to manage badges for [projects](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/badges/) and [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/badges/#group-badges).

## Placeholders

Badges support placeholders that are replaced in real time in both the link and image URL.
The following placeholders are available:

- `%{project_path}`: replaced by the project path.
- `%{project_title}`: replaced by the project title.
- `%{project_name}`: replaced by the project name.
- `%{project_id}`: replaced by the project ID.
- `%{project_namespace}`: replaced by the project's namespace full path.
- `%{group_name}`: replaced by the project's top-level group name.
- `%{gitlab_server}`: replaced by the project's server name.
- `%{gitlab_pages_domain}`: replaced by the domain name hosting GitLab Pages.
- `%{default_branch}`: replaced by the project default branch.
- `%{commit_sha}`: replaced by the project's last commit SHA.
- `%{latest_tag}`: replaced by the project's last tag.

Group badge endpoints operate outside a project's context, so placeholder values are taken from the
group's earliest-created project. If no projects exist in the group, the URL is returned unchanged.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/group_badges/">External documentation</a>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-batched-background-migrations">Batched background migrations</h1>

Use this API to list, retrieve, pause, and resume the
[batched background migrations](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/background_migrations/) running on an instance.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

## Retrieve a batched background migration

<a id="opIdgetApiV4AdminBatchedBackgroundMigrationsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/admin/batched_background_migrations/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/admin/batched_background_migrations/{id}`

Fetches details of a specific batched migration, with optional filtering by database target.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-batched-background-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the batched background migration.|
|database|query|string|false|Name of the database.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|database|main|
|database|ci|
|database|sec|
|database|embedding|
|database|geo|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "1234",
  "job_class_name": "CopyColumnUsingBackgroundMigrationJob",
  "table_name": "events",
  "column_name": "id",
  "status": "active",
  "progress": 50,
  "created_at": "2022-11-28T16:26:39+02:00",
  "estimated_time_remaining": "1 day"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesBatchedBackgroundMigration](#schemaapientitiesbatchedbackgroundmigration)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|401 Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|403 Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|404 Not found|None|

## Restart a batched background operation

<a id="opIdputApiV4AdminBatchedBackgroundOperationsIdRestart"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/admin/batched_background_operations/0/restart \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "database": "main"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/admin/batched_background_operations/{id}/restart`

This feature was introduced in GitLab 19.2.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "database": "main"
}
```

<h3 id="restart-a-batched-background-operation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the batched background operation.|
|body|body|[putApiV4AdminBatchedBackgroundOperationsIdRestartRequest](#schemaputapiv4adminbatchedbackgroundoperationsidrestartrequest)|false|none|
|» database|body|string|false|Name of the database.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-boards">Boards</h1>

Use this API to manage [issue boards](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issue_board/) and their lists, for both projects and [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issue_board/#group-issue-boards).

Every call to this API requires authentication. If the project or group is private and the
authenticated user is not a member, a `GET` request results in a `404` status code.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/boards/">External documentation</a>

## Update a group issue board

<a id="opIdputApiV4GroupsIdBoardsBoardId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/string/boards/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "hide_backlog_list": true,
    "hide_closed_list": true,
    "assignee_id": 0,
    "milestone_id": 0,
    "labels": "string",
    "weight": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/groups/{id}/boards/{board_id}`

Updates a specified group issue board.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "hide_backlog_list": true,
  "hide_closed_list": true,
  "assignee_id": 0,
  "milestone_id": 0,
  "labels": "string",
  "weight": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-group-issue-board-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|board_id|path|integer|true|ID of the board.|
|body|body|[putApiV4GroupsIdBoardsBoardIdRequest](#schemaputapiv4groupsidboardsboardidrequest)|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the board.|
|» hide_backlog_list|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, hides the Open list.|
|» hide_closed_list|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, hides the Closed list.|
|» assignee_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the assignee to scope the board to. Premium and Ultimate only.|
|» milestone_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of a milestone to associate with board|
|» labels|body|string \| null|false|Comma-separated list of label names|
|» weight|body|integer \| null|false|The weight of the board|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
```

## Create a group issue board list

<a id="opIdpostApiV4GroupsIdBoardsBoardIdLists"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/string/boards/0/lists \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label_id": 0,
    "milestone_id": 0,
    "iteration_id": 0,
    "assignee_id": 0,
    "status_id": 0
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/groups/{id}/boards/{board_id}/lists`

Creates a group issue board list for a specified board.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label_id": 0,
  "milestone_id": 0,
  "iteration_id": 0,
  "assignee_id": 0,
  "status_id": 0
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-group-issue-board-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|
|board_id|path|integer|true|ID of the board.|
|body|body|[postApiV4GroupsIdBoardsBoardIdListsRequest](#schemapostapiv4groupsidboardsboardidlistsrequest)|false|none|
|» label_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the label. Exactly one of `label_id`, `milestone_id`, `iteration_id`, `assignee_id`, `status_id` must be provided.|
|» milestone_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of an existing milestone. Exactly one of `label_id`, `milestone_id`, `iteration_id`, `assignee_id`, `status_id` must be provided.|
|» iteration_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the iteration. Premium and Ultimate only. Exactly one of `label_id`, `milestone_id`, `iteration_id`, `assignee_id`, `status_id` must be provided.|
|» assignee_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the user. Premium and Ultimate only. Exactly one of `label_id`, `milestone_id`, `iteration_id`, `assignee_id`, `status_id` must be provided.|
|» status_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the status. Premium and Ultimate only. Exactly one of `label_id`, `milestone_id`, `iteration_id`, `assignee_id`, `status_id` must be provided.|

## Update an issue board

<a id="opIdputApiV4ProjectsIdBoardsBoardId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/boards/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "hide_backlog_list": true,
    "hide_closed_list": true,
    "assignee_id": 0,
    "milestone_id": 0,
    "labels": "string",
    "weight": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/projects/{id}/boards/{board_id}`

Updates a specified issue board in a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "hide_backlog_list": true,
  "hide_closed_list": true,
  "assignee_id": 0,
  "milestone_id": 0,
  "labels": "string",
  "weight": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-issue-board-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|board_id|path|integer|true|ID of the board.|
|body|body|[putApiV4ProjectsIdBoardsBoardIdRequest](#schemaputapiv4projectsidboardsboardidrequest)|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the board.|
|» hide_backlog_list|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, hides the Open list.|
|» hide_closed_list|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, hides the Closed list.|
|» assignee_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the assignee to scope the board to. Premium and Ultimate only.|
|» milestone_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of a milestone to associate with board|
|» labels|body|string \| null|false|Comma-separated list of label names|
|» weight|body|integer \| null|false|The weight of the board|

```bash
  "milestone_id": 0,
```

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-branches">Branches</h1>

Use this API to manage [Git branches](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/branches/).

To change the branch protections configured for a project, use the [protected branches API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/protected_branches/).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/branches/">External documentation</a>

## List all repository branches

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryBranches"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/repository/branches \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/branches`

Lists all repository branches from a specified project, sorted alphabetically by name. Search by name, or use regular expressions to find specific branch patterns. Returns detailed information about the branch, including its protection status, merge status, and commit details.

<h3 id="list-all-repository-branches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Return branches containing the search string. Use `^term` to find branches that begin with `term`, and `term$` to find branches that end with `term`.|
|regex|query|string \| null|false|Return branches with names matching an [RE2](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax) regular expression. Cannot be used together with `search`.|
|sort|query|string \| null|false|Sort results by the specified field and direction.|
|page_token|query|string \| null|false|Name of the branch to start the pagination from. Used for keyset pagination.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|name_asc|
|sort|updated_asc|
|sort|updated_desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "name": "master",
    "commit": {
      "id": "2695effb5807a22ff3d138d593fd856244e155e7",
      "short_id": "2695effb",
      "created_at": "2017-07-26T11:08:53.000+02:00",
      "parent_ids": [
        "2a4b78934375d7f53875269ffd4f45fd83a84ebe"
      ],
      "title": "Initial commit",
      "message": "Initial commit",
      "author_name": "John Smith",
      "author_email": "john@example.com",
      "authored_date": "2012-05-28T04:42:42-07:00",
      "committer_name": "Jack Smith",
      "committer_email": "jack@example.com",
      "committed_date": "2012-05-28T04:42:42-07:00",
      "trailers": {
        "Merged-By": "Jane Doe janedoe@gitlab.com"
      },
      "extended_trailers": {
        "Signed-off-by": [
          "John Doe <johndoe@gitlab.com>",
          "Jane Doe <janedoe@gitlab.com>"
        ]
      },
      "web_url": "https://gitlab.example.com/janedoe/gitlab-foss/-/commit/ed899a2f4b50b4370feeea94676502b42383c746"

  }
]
```

## Protect a single branch

<a id="opIdputApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryBranchesBranchProtect"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/repository/branches/string/protect \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "developers_can_push": true,
    "developers_can_merge": true
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/branches/{branch}/protect`

Protects a single branch, or updates its protection if it is already protected. Only users with the Maintainer role can push or merge unless `developers_can_push` or `developers_can_merge` is `true`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "developers_can_push": true,
  "developers_can_merge": true
}
```

<h3 id="protect-a-single-branch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|branch|path|string|true|Name of the branch.|
|body|body|[putApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryBranchesBranchProtectRequest](#schemaputapiv4projectsidrepositorybranchesbranchprotectrequest)|false|none|
|» developers_can_push|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, allows developers to push to the branch.|
|» developers_can_merge|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, allows developers to merge to the branch.|

> Example responses

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-broadcast-messages">Broadcast messages</h1>

Use this API to interact with banners and notifications displayed in the UI. For more information, see [broadcast messages](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/broadcast_messages/).

GET requests do not require authentication. All other broadcast message API endpoints are accessible only to administrators. Non-GET requests by:

- Unauthenticated users result in `401 Unauthorized`.
- Authenticated non-administrators result in `403 Forbidden`.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/broadcast_messages/">External documentation</a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-ci-catalog">CI catalog</h1>

Use this API to publish a release of a component project to the
[CI/CD catalog](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/components/).

This endpoint is intended for CLI tooling and must be authenticated with a
[job token](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/ci_job_token/).

## Publish a new component project release as version to the CI/CD catalog

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdCatalogPublish"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/catalog/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "metadata": {}
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/catalog/publish`

Publishes a release of a catalog resource as version to the CI/CD catalog.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "metadata": {}
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdCatalogPublishRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidcatalogpublishrequest)|true|none|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|true|Metadata for the release.|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-ci-jobs">CI jobs</h1>

Use this API to interact with [CI/CD jobs](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/jobs/">External documentation</a>

## List all jobs for a project

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/jobs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/jobs`

Lists all jobs for a specified project. By default, this request returns 20 results at a time because the API results are paginated.

<h3 id="list-all-jobs-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|scope|query|[string]|false|Filter jobs by status. Accepts a single value or an array of values. If omitted, returns all jobs.|
|ref|query|string \| null|false|Branch name (ref) to filter jobs by.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|created|
|scope|waiting_for_resource|
|scope|preparing|
|scope|waiting_for_callback|
|scope|pending|
|scope|running|
|scope|success|
|scope|failed|
|scope|canceling|
|scope|canceled|
|scope|skipped|
|scope|manual|
|scope|scheduled|
