## Update a release

<a id="opIdputApiV4ProjectsIdReleasesTagName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/releases/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "released_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "milestones": [
      "string"
    ],
    "milestone_ids": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/projects/{id}/releases/{tag_name}`

Updates a release. Developer level access to the project is required to update a release.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "released_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "milestones": [
    "string"
  ],
  "milestone_ids": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|tag_name|path|string|true|Git tag the release is associated with.|
|body|body|[putApiV4ProjectsIdReleasesTagNameRequest](#schemaputapiv4projectsidreleasestagnamerequest)|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the release.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the release. You can use [Markdown](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/markdown/).|
|» released_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Date when the release is or was ready.|
|» milestones|body|[string]|false|Title of each milestone to associate with the release. [GitLab Premium](https://about.gitlab.com/pricing/) customers can specify group milestones. Cannot be combined with the `milestone_ids` parameter. To remove all milestones from the release, specify `[]`. Mutually exclusive with `milestone_ids`.|
|» milestone_ids|body|string \| null \| integer \| null|false|ID of each milestone the release is associated with. GitLab Premium customers can specify group milestones. Cannot be combined with the `milestones` parameter. To remove all milestones from the release, specify `[]`. Mutually exclusive with `milestones`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer \| null|false|none|

## Delete a release

<a id="opIddeleteApiV4ProjectsIdReleasesTagName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/releases/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/v4/projects/{id}/releases/{tag_name}`

Delete a release. Deleting a release doesn't delete the associated tag. Requires at least the Developer role for the project. This feature was introduced in GitLab 11.7.

<h3 id="delete-a-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|tag_name|path|string|true|Git tag the release is associated with.|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-remote-mirrors">Remote mirrors</h1>

Use this API to manage [remote mirrors](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/mirror/push/).
You can query and modify the state of these mirrors.

For security reasons, the `url` attribute in the API response is always scrubbed of username
and password information.

> [!note]
> [Pull mirrors](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/mirror/pull/) use
> [a different API endpoint](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/project_pull_mirroring/#update-project-pull-mirroring-settings) to
> display and update them.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/remote_mirrors/">External documentation</a>

## Create a push mirror

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdRemoteMirrors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/remote_mirrors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://*****:*****@example.com/gitlab/example.git",

    "auth_method": "ssh_public_key",
    "keep_divergent_refs": true,
    "only_protected_branches": true,
    "mirror_branch_regex": "string",
    "host_keys": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/remote_mirrors`

Creates a push mirror.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://*****:*****@example.com/gitlab/example.git",
  "enabled": true,
  "auth_method": "ssh_public_key",
  "keep_divergent_refs": true,
  "only_protected_branches": true,
  "mirror_branch_regex": "string",
  "host_keys": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-push-mirror-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdRemoteMirrorsRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidremotemirrorsrequest)|true|none|
|» url|body|string \| null|true|Target URL to which the repository is mirrored.|
|» enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, the mirror is enabled.|
|» auth_method|body|string \| null|false|Mirror authentication method.|
|» keep_divergent_refs|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, divergent refs are kept when mirroring.|
|» only_protected_branches|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, only protected branches are mirrored. Mutually exclusive with `mirror_branch_regex`.|
|» mirror_branch_regex|body|string \| null|false|Determines if only matched branches are mirrored. Mutually exclusive with `only_protected_branches`.|
|» host_keys|body|[string]|false|SSH host keys in bare format, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA...`, or full `known_hosts` format, such as `hostname ssh-ed25519 AAAA...`. Bare keys use the hostname from the mirror URL.|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-repositories">Repositories</h1>

Use this API to manage [Git repositories](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/).

## List all repository trees in a project

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryTree"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/1/repository/tree \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/tree`

Lists all repository files and directories in a specified project. This endpoint can be accessed without authentication if the repository is publicly accessible. This command provides essentially the same features as the `git ls-tree` command. Use `with_last_commit` to include the last commit that changed each entry. `with_last_commit` cannot be combined with `recursive`.

<h3 id="list-all-repository-trees-in-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|ref|query|string \| null|false|Name of a repository branch or tag. If omitted, uses the default branch.|
|path|query|string \| null|false|Path inside the repository, used to get the contents of subdirectories.|
|recursive|query|boolean|false|If `true`, returns a recursive tree.|
|with_last_commit|query|boolean|false|If `true`, includes the last commit for each tree entry. Cannot be combined with `recursive`. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/234455) in GitLab 19.3.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|
|pagination|query|string|false|Pagination method. `keyset` uses the [keyset-based pagination method](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/#keyset-based-pagination). `none` is valid only if `recursive` is `true`.|
|page_token|query|string \| null|false|Tree record ID at which to fetch the next page. Used only with keyset pagination.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|pagination|legacy|
|pagination|keyset|
|pagination|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "a1e8f8d745cc87e3a9248358d9352bb7f9a0aeba",
  "name": "html",
  "type": "tree",
  "path": "files/html",
  "mode": "040000",
  "last_commit": {
    "id": "2695effb5807a22ff3d138d593fd856244e155e7",
    "short_id": "2695effb",
    "created_at": "2017-07-26T11:08:53.000+02:00",
    "parent_ids": [
      "2a4b78934375d7f53875269ffd4f45fd83a84ebe"
    ],
    "title": "Initial commit",
    "message": "Initial commit",
    "author_name": "John Smith",
    "author_email": "john@example.com",
    "authored_date": "2012-05-28T04:42:42-07:00",
    "committer_name": "Jack Smith",
    "committer_email": "jack@example.com",
    "committed_date": "2012-05-28T04:42:42-07:00",
    "trailers": {
      "Merged-By": "Jane Doe janedoe@gitlab.com"
    },
    "extended_trailers": {
      "Signed-off-by": [
        "John Doe <johndoe@gitlab.com>",
        "Jane Doe <janedoe@gitlab.com>"
      ]
    },
    "web_url": "https://gitlab.example.com/janedoe/gitlab-foss/-/commit/ed899a2f4b50b4370feeea94676502b42383c746"
  }
}
```

|format|query|string \| null|false|Archive format.|
|path|query|string \| null|false|Subpath of the repository to download. An empty string returns the whole repository.|
|include_lfs_blobs|query|boolean|false|If `true`, LFS objects are included in the archive. When set to `false`, LFS objects are excluded.|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/compare`

Compares branches, tags, or commits. Retrieves the differences between two branches, tags, or commits in a specified project.

<h3 id="compare-branches-tags-or-commits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|from|query|string \| null|true|Ref to compare from. Accepts a commit SHA, branch name, or tag name.|
|to|query|string \| null|true|Ref to compare to. Accepts a commit SHA, branch name, or tag name.|
|from_project_id|query|integer \| null|false|ID of the project to compare from.|
|straight|query|boolean|false|If `true`, comparison method is direct comparison between `from` and `to` (`from`..`to`). If `false`, compares using merge base (`from`...`to`).|
|unidiff|query|boolean|false|If `true`, presents diffs in the [unified diff](https://www.gnu.org/software/diffutils/manual/html_node/Detailed-Unified.html) format.|

## Get contents of multiple files in a single request

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryBlobsBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/1/repository/blobs/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "files": [
      {
        "path": "app/models/user.rb",
        "ref": "main"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/blobs/batch`

Each blob is truncated to the first 1 MB; the `truncated` field indicates when this happens.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "app/models/user.rb",
      "ref": "main"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-contents-of-multiple-files-in-a-single-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryBlobsBatchRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidrepositoryblobsbatchrequest)|true|none|
|» files|body|[object]|true|Array of file objects to retrieve, up to a maximum of 20.|
|» » path|body|string \| null|true|Path of the file in the repository.|
|» » ref|body|string \| null|false|Branch, tag, or commit to read the file from. Defaults to the default branch.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "path": "app/models/user.rb",
    "ref": "main",
    "size": 1476,
    "truncated": false,
    "encoding": "base64",
    "content": "VGhpcyBpcyBhIGZpbGU="
  }
]
```

## Generate changelog data

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryChangelog"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/1/repository/changelog?version=1.0.0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/changelog`

Generates changelog data based on commits in a repository, without committing them to a changelog file. Works exactly like `POST /projects/:id/repository/changelog`, except the changelog data is not committed to any changelog file.

<h3 id="generate-changelog-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|version|query|string \| null|true|Version to generate the changelog for. Must follow [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/) format.|
|from|query|string \| null|false|First commit in the range of commits, as a SHA, to use for the changelog. This commit is not included in the changelog. If omitted, the most recent stable version tag before `version` is used.|
|to|query|string \| null|false|Last commit in the range of commits, as a SHA, to use for the changelog. This commit is included in the changelog. If omitted, uses the latest commit on the default branch. For the Add changelog data to file operation, uses the latest commit on `branch` instead. The range can contain at most 15,000 commits.|
|date|query|string(date-time) \| null|false|Date and time of the release. Defaults to the current time.|
|trailer|query|string|false|Git trailer to use for including commits. Case-sensitive: `Example` does not match `example` or `eXaMpLE`.|
|config_file|query|string \| null|false|Path to the changelog configuration file in the project's Git repository. If omitted, uses `.gitlab/changelog_config.yml`.|
|config_file_ref|query|string \| null|false|Git reference, for example a branch, where the changelog configuration file is defined. Defaults to the default branch of the repository.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "notes": "## 1.0.0 (2023-01-01)"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-changelog-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesChangelog](#schemaapientitieschangelog)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/changelog`

|» from|body|string \| null|false|First commit in the range of commits, as a SHA, to use for the changelog. This commit is not included in the changelog. If omitted, the most recent stable version tag before `version` is used.|
|» to|body|string \| null|false|Last commit in the range of commits, as a SHA, to use for the changelog. This commit is included in the changelog. If omitted, uses the latest commit on the default branch. For the Add changelog data to file operation, uses the latest commit on `branch` instead. The range can contain at most 15,000 commits.|
|» date|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Date and time of the release. Defaults to the current time.|
|» trailer|body|string|false|Git trailer to use for including commits. Case-sensitive: `Example` does not match `example` or `eXaMpLE`.|
|» config_file|body|string \| null|false|Path to the changelog configuration file in the project's Git repository. If omitted, uses `.gitlab/changelog_config.yml`.|
|» config_file_ref|body|string \| null|false|Git reference, for example a branch, where the changelog configuration file is defined. Defaults to the default branch of the repository.|
|» branch|body|string \| null|false|Name of the branch to commit the changelog changes to. If omitted, defaults to the project's default branch.|
|» file|body|string|false|File to commit the changes to.|
|» message|body|string \| null|false|Commit message to use when committing the changelog changes. If omitted, defaults to `Add changelog for version X`, where `X` is the value of the `version` parameter.|

<h3 id="add-changelog-data-to-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-resource-events">Resource events</h1>

Use this API to retrieve the events that track changes to issues, merge requests, and epics:

- [Label](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/labels/) events record who added or removed a label, and when.
- [Iteration](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/iterations/) events record iteration changes for issues.
- Milestone events record milestone changes for issues and merge requests.
- State events record state changes for issues, merge requests, and epics.
- Weight events record weight changes for issues.

State events do not track the initial state (`created` or `opened`) of a resource. For a resource
that was never closed or reopened, an empty list is returned.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/resource_label_events/">External documentation</a>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-resource-subscriptions">Resource subscriptions</h1>

Use this API to subscribe to and unsubscribe from [issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/),
[merge requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/), and
[labels](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/labels/) in projects and groups.

All API calls to non-public information require authentication.

## Subscribe to a merge request

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdMergeRequestsSubscribableIdSubscribe"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/merge_requests/string/subscribe \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/merge_requests/{subscribable_id}/subscribe`

Subscribes the currently authenticated user to a specified merge request. They will receive notifications on changes to this item.

<h3 id="subscribe-to-a-merge-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|subscribable_id|path|string|true|Internal ID of the issue or merge request, or ID or title of the label.|

## Unsubscribe to a merge request

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdMergeRequestsSubscribableIdUnsubscribe"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/merge_requests/string/unsubscribe \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/merge_requests/{subscribable_id}/unsubscribe`

Unsubscribes the currently authenticated user from a specified merge request. They will no longer receive notifications on changes to this item.

<h3 id="unsubscribe-to-a-merge-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|subscribable_id|path|string|true|Internal ID of the issue or merge request, or ID or title of the label.|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-rollouts">Rollouts</h1>

Operations related to rollouts.

## Ingest a rollout workflow event

<a id="opIdpostApiV4RolloutsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/rollouts/1 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "topic": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "data": {
      "position": [
        0
      ],
      "stage_name": "string",
      "environment": "string",
      "step_type": "string",
      "service": "string",
      "error": "string",
      "reason": "string",
      "reply": "string"
    },
    "value": {},
    "channel_tokens": [
      {
        "channel_name": "string",
        "token": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/rollouts/{id}`

Reports flow-graph progress from the CD orchestrator (a Starlark workflow run by AutoFlow).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "topic": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "data": {
    "position": [
      0
    ],
    "stage_name": "string",
    "environment": "string",
    "step_type": "string",
    "service": "string",
    "error": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "reply": "string"
  },
  "value": {},
  "channel_tokens": [
    {
      "channel_name": "string",
      "token": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="ingest-a-rollout-workflow-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|The ID of the rollout|
|body|body|[postApiV4RolloutsIdRequest](#schemapostapiv4rolloutsidrequest)|false|none|
|» topic|body|string \| null|false|The event topic|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|The event type|
|» data|body|object \| null|false|The event payload. Exactly one of `data`, `value` must be provided.|
|» » position|body|[integer]|false|Zero-based path to the stage/step in the flow definition; required for every event except com.gitlab.cd.rollout_succeeded|
|» » stage_name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the enclosing stage (an environment tier); absent for a step outside any stage|
|» » environment|body|string \| null|false|Exact name of the target GitLab environment; resolves the rollout environment to update when a stage deploys to more than one environment|
|» » step_type|body|string \| null|false|The step type, present on step_* events|
|» » service|body|string \| null|false|Name of the Cd::Service, present on service_started/service_succeeded/service_failed|
|» » error|body|string \| null|false|Failure detail, present on step_failed and service_failed|
|» » reason|body|string \| null|false|Human-readable prompt, present on approval_requested|
|» » reply|body|string \| null|false|Name of the AutoFlow channel to post the approval decision back into, present on approval_requested|
|» value|body|object \| null|false|AutoFlow Value (protojson), decoded into the same topic/type/data shape as `data` above. Exactly one of `data`, `value` must be provided.|
|» channel_tokens|body|[object]|false|AutoFlow channels opened alongside this event, for posting a value back into them later|
|» » channel_name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the AutoFlow channel|
|» » token|body|string \| null|true|Token used to post a value into the channel|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
```

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-runner-controller-tokens">Runner controller tokens</h1>

Use this API to create, list, rotate, and revoke the authentication tokens that runner controllers
use to authenticate with a GitLab instance and manage runners.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

> [!note]
> The availability of these endpoints is controlled by a feature flag. They are available for
> testing, but not ready for production use.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/runner_controller_tokens/">External documentation</a>

## Create a runner controller token

<a id="opIdpostApiV4RunnerControllersRunnerControllerIdTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/runner_controllers/0/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Token for managing runner"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/runner_controllers/{runner_controller_id}/tokens`

Creates a runner controller token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Token for managing runner"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-runner-controller-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runner_controller_id|path|integer|true|ID of the runner controller.|
|body|body|[postApiV4RunnerControllersRunnerControllerIdTokensRequest](#schemapostapiv4runnercontrollersrunnercontrolleridtokensrequest)|false|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the runner controller token.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "runner_controller_id": 1,
  "description": "Controller for managing runner",
  "last_used_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-runner-controller-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not found|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-runner-controllers">Runner controllers</h1>

Use this API to manage the runner controllers that handle CI/CD job admission control, and the scopes
assigned to them. Runner controllers connect to the job router and evaluate jobs against custom
policies, deciding whether to admit or reject them.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

> [!note]
> The availability of these endpoints is controlled by a feature flag. They are available for
> testing, but not ready for production use.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/runner_controllers/">External documentation</a>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

Lists all scopes for a runner controller.

|---|---|---|---|---|

<h3 id="list-all-scopes-for-a-runner-controller-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|

## Add instance scope

<a id="opIdpostApiV4RunnerControllersIdScopesInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/runner_controllers/0/scopes/instance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/v4/runner_controllers/{id}/scopes/instance`

Adds an instance scope to a runner controller. When added, the runner controller evaluates jobs for all runners in the GitLab instance. A runner controller can have only one instance scope. If an instance scope already exists, this operation returns an error.

<h3 id="add-instance-scope-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the runner controller.|

```json
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not found|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|

## Update a runner

<a id="opIdputApiV4RunnersId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/runners/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "active": true,
    "paused": true,
    "tag_list": [
      "string"
    ],
    "run_untagged": true,
    "locked": true,
    "access_level": "not_protected",
    "maximum_timeout": 0,
    "maintenance_note": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/runners/{id}`

Updates a specified runner.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "active": true,
  "paused": true,
  "tag_list": [
    "string"
  ],
  "run_untagged": true,
  "locked": true,
  "access_level": "not_protected",
  "maximum_timeout": 0,
  "maintenance_note": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-runner-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the runner.|
|body|body|[putApiV4RunnersIdRequest](#schemaputapiv4runnersidrequest)|false|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the runner. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» active|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, the runner is allowed to receive jobs. Deprecated. Use `paused` instead. Mutually exclusive with `paused`. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» paused|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, the runner ignores new jobs. Mutually exclusive with `active`. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» tag_list|body|[string]|false|List of tags for the runner. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» run_untagged|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, the runner can execute untagged jobs. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» locked|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, the runner is locked. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» access_level|body|string \| null|false|Access level of the runner. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» maximum_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|Maximum time, in seconds, that runners can spend running a job. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|
|» maintenance_note|body|string \| null|false|Free-form maintenance notes for the runner. Limited to 1024 characters. At least one of `description`, `active`, `paused`, `tag_list`, `run_untagged`, `locked`, `access_level`, `maximum_timeout`, `maintenance_note` must be provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» access_level|not_protected|
|» access_level|ref_protected|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-saml-group-links">SAML group links</h1>

Use this API to manage the [SAML group links](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/saml_sso/group_sync/)
that map a group in your identity provider to a GitLab group, and to the role its members receive.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/saml/">External documentation</a>

## Lists SAML group links

<a id="opIdgetApiV4GroupsIdSamlGroupLinks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/groups/string/saml_group_links \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/groups/{id}/saml_group_links`

Get SAML group links for a group

<h3 id="lists-saml-group-links-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the group.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "name": "saml-group-1",
    "access_level": 40,
    "member_role_id": 12,
    "provider": "saml"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="lists-saml-group-links-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-search">Search</h1>

Use this API to [search across GitLab](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/) in an instance, a group,
or a project, and to retrieve information about
[advanced search migrations](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/advanced_search/elasticsearch/#advanced-search-migrations).

Every call to this API requires authentication. Retrieving advanced search migrations requires
administrator access.

Some scopes are available for [basic search](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/#available-scopes).
When [advanced search](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/advanced_search/#available-scopes) or
[exact code search](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/exact_code_search/#available-scopes) is
enabled, additional scopes become available. To use basic search instead, see
[specify a search type](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/#specify-a-search-type).

These endpoints support [offset-based pagination](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/#offset-based-pagination).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/search/">External documentation</a>

## Search project code using natural language

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdDashSearchSemantic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/(-/)search/semantic?q=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/(-/)search/semantic`

Introduced in GitLab 18.11.

Searches indexed project code using semantic (meaning-based) similarity rather than
keyword matching. Use this when you do not know the exact symbol or file name, or
to discover how a behavior is implemented across the codebase.

Primary use cases:
- When you do not know the exact symbol or file path
- To see how a behavior or feature is implemented across the codebase
- To discover related implementations (clients, jobs, workers)

How to use:
- Provide a concise, specific query with concrete keywords
- Use directory_path to narrow scope (e.g. "app/services/")
- Prefer precise intent over broad terms

Results are grouped by file. Each file includes merged line ranges with content
and a relevance score (0.0-1.0). The response includes an overall confidence
level (high/medium/low/unknown) based on score distribution. Results are
filtered by Duo context exclusion settings.

Requires semantic code search to be enabled and indexed for the project namespace.


<h3 id="search-project-code-using-natural-language-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|q|query|string \| null|true|Natural language search query, for example `authentication middleware` or `rate limiting logic`.|
|directory_path|query|string \| null|false|Restrict search to files under this directory path, for example `app/services/`. Must be a relative path with no leading slash and no `..` segments.|
|knn|query|integer|false|Number of nearest neighbours to retrieve internally (default: 64). Higher values improve recall at the cost of latency.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of results to return (default: 20).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "confidence": "high",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "app/models/user.rb",
      "blob_id": "abc123def456",
      "file_url": "https://gitlab.com/group/project/-/blob/main/user.rb",
      "score": 0.92,
      "snippet_ranges": [
        {
          "start_line": 42,
          "end_line": 44,
          "content": "def authenticate\n  ...\nend",
          "score": 0.85
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="search-project-code-using-natural-language-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesAiSemanticCodeResponse](#schemaapientitiesaisemanticcoderesponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not found - project not found or semantic code search unavailable|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity - project has no embeddings|None|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable - search backend timed out|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Search an instance

<a id="opIdgetApiV4Search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/search?search=string&scope=wiki_blobs' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/search`

Searches for a term across the entire GitLab instance. The response depends on the requested scope.

<h3 id="search-an-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|search|query|string \| null|true|Search query.|
|scope|query|string|true|Scope of the search.|
|state|query|string \| null|false|Filter results by state. Applies only to the `issues`, `work_items`, and `merge_requests` scopes.|
|confidential|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, returns only confidential results. If `false`, returns only non-confidential results. Applies only to the `issues` and `work_items` scopes.|
|type|query|[string]|false|Filter work items by type. Only applies to work_items scope. Available types: issue, task, epic, incident, test_case, requirement, objective, key_result, ticket.|
|include_archived|query|boolean|false|If `true`, includes archived projects in the search. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/493281) in GitLab 18.7.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|Fields to search. Supports only `issues` and `merge_requests` scopes. Premium and Ultimate only.|
|exclude_forks|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, excludes forked projects from the search. If omitted, forks are excluded. Available for exact code search. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/493281) in GitLab 18.7.|
|num_context_lines|query|integer \| null|false|Number of context lines to include around each match in the results. Available for advanced and exact code search only. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/583217) in GitLab 18.11.|
|regex|query|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, uses regular expressions to search for code. If omitted, regular expressions are used. Available for exact code search. [Introduced](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/521686) in GitLab 18.9.|
|source_branch|query|string \| null|false|Filter merge requests by source branch. Available with advanced search and the merge_requests scope.|
|target_branch|query|string \| null|false|Filter merge requests by target branch. Available with advanced search and the merge_requests scope.|
|author_username|query|string \| null|false|Filter by author username. A username that matches no user is ignored. Available with advanced search and the issues, merge_requests and work_items scopes.|
|label_name|query|[string]|false|Filter by label name. A result must carry every name that resolves to an existing label; names that match no label are ignored. Maximum 30 names. Available with advanced search and the issues, merge_requests and work_items scopes.|
|not|query|object \| null|false|Filter out results matching the parameters supplied. Supplying a filter together with its negation matches either condition, which widens the result set.|
|not[source_branch]|query|string \| null|false|Exclude merge requests with this source branch|
|not[target_branch]|query|string \| null|false|Exclude merge requests with this target branch|
|not[author_username]|query|string \| null|false|Exclude results authored by this username|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|wiki_blobs|
|scope|blobs|
|scope|commits|
|scope|notes|
|scope|projects|
|scope|groups|
|scope|issues|
|scope|work_items|
|scope|merge_requests|
|scope|milestones|
|scope|snippet_titles|
|scope|users|
|state|all|
|state|opened|
|state|closed|
|state|merged|
|fields|title|

<h3 id="search-an-instance-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|

http, oauth2, apiKey

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-security-scans">Security scans</h1>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-service-accounts">Service accounts</h1>

Use this API to interact with [service accounts](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/service_accounts/).

The number of service accounts you can create depends on your subscription and offering:

- On GitLab Premium and Ultimate, you can create an unlimited number of service accounts for all offerings.
- On GitLab Free, limits vary by offering:
  - For GitLab.com, you can create up to 100 service accounts for each top-level group.
    This includes service accounts created in subgroups or projects.
  - For GitLab Self-Managed, you can create up to 100 service accounts for the entire instance.
    This includes service accounts created for the instance, a group, or a project.

You can also interact with service accounts through the [users API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/users/).
To manage SSH keys for service accounts, use the [user SSH and GPG keys API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/user_keys/).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/service_accounts/">External documentation</a>

`POST /api/v4/snippets`

Creates a snippet.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "visibility": "internal",
  "files": [

      "file_path": "string",
      "content": "string"
    }
  ],
  "content": "string",
  "file_name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-snippet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[postApiV4SnippetsRequest](#schemapostapiv4snippetsrequest)|true|none|
|» title|body|string \| null|true|Title of the snippet.|

|» visibility|body|string|false|Visibility level for the snippet. On GitLab.com, the `internal` value is not available.|

|» » content|body|string \| null|true|Content of the snippet file.|
|» content|body|string \| null|false|The content of a snippet. Mutually exclusive with `files`. Exactly one of `files`, `content` must be provided.|
|» file_name|body|string \| null|true|The name of a snippet file|

## Update snippet

<a id="opIdputApiV4SnippetsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/snippets/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "content": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "file_name": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "visibility": "private",
    "files": [
      {
        "action": "create",
        "content": "string",
        "file_path": "string",
        "previous_path": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/snippets/{id}`

Updates a specified snippet.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "file_name": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "visibility": "private",
  "files": [
    {
      "action": "create",
      "content": "string",
      "file_path": "string",
      "previous_path": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-snippet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the snippet.|
|body|body|[putApiV4SnippetsIdRequest](#schemaputapiv4snippetsidrequest)|false|none|
|» content|body|string \| null|false|The content of a snippet. Mutually exclusive with `files`. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the snippet. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» file_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of a snippet file. Mutually exclusive with `files`. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|Title of the snippet. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» visibility|body|string \| null|false|Visibility level for the snippet. On GitLab.com, the `internal` value is not available. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» files|body|[object]|false|Array of files to update for the snippet. Required when the snippet has multiple files. Mutually exclusive with `content`, `file_name`. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» » action|body|string|true|The type of action to perform on the file, must be one of: create, update, delete, move|
|» » content|body|string \| null|false|Content of the snippet file.|
|» » file_path|body|string \| null|false|Path of the snippet file.|
|» » previous_path|body|string \| null|false|Previous path of the snippet file.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|internal|
|» visibility|public|
|» » action|create|
|» » action|update|
|» » action|delete|
|» » action|move|

|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdSnippetsRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidsnippetsrequest)|true|none|
|» title|body|string \| null|true|Title of the snippet.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the snippet.|
|» visibility|body|string|true|Visibility level for the snippet. On GitLab.com, the `internal` value is not available.|
|» files|body|[object]|false|Array of files for the snippet. Mutually exclusive with `content`. Exactly one of `files`, `content` must be provided.|
|» » file_path|body|string \| null|true|Path of the snippet file.|
|» » content|body|string \| null|true|Content of the snippet file.|
|» content|body|string \| null|false|The content of a snippet. Mutually exclusive with `files`. Exactly one of `files`, `content` must be provided.|
|» file_name|body|string \| null|true|The name of a snippet file|

|---|---|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|internal|
|» visibility|public|

## Update a project snippet

<a id="opIdputApiV4ProjectsIdSnippetsSnippetId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/snippets/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "content": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "file_name": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "visibility": "private",
    "files": [
      {
        "action": "create",
        "content": "string",
        "file_path": "string",
        "previous_path": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/projects/{id}/snippets/{snippet_id}`

Updates a specified project snippet. The user must have permission to modify snippets. Updates to snippets with multiple files must use the `files` attribute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "file_name": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "visibility": "private",
  "files": [
    {
      "action": "create",
      "content": "string",
      "file_path": "string",
      "previous_path": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-project-snippet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|snippet_id|path|integer|true|ID of the snippet.|
|body|body|[putApiV4ProjectsIdSnippetsSnippetIdRequest](#schemaputapiv4projectsidsnippetssnippetidrequest)|false|none|
|» content|body|string \| null|false|Content of the snippet. Deprecated. Use `files` instead. Mutually exclusive with `files`. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the snippet. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» file_name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the snippet file. Deprecated. Use `files` instead. Mutually exclusive with `files`. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|Title of the snippet. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» visibility|body|string \| null|false|Visibility level for the snippet. On GitLab.com, the `internal` value is not available. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» files|body|[object]|false|Array of files to update for the snippet. Required when the snippet has multiple files. Mutually exclusive with `content`, `file_name`. At least one of `content`, `description`, `files`, `file_name`, `title`, `visibility` must be provided.|
|» » action|body|string|true|The type of action to perform on the file, must be one of: create, update, delete, move|
|» » content|body|string \| null|false|Content of the snippet file.|
|» » file_path|body|string \| null|false|Path of the snippet file.|
|» » previous_path|body|string \| null|false|Previous path of the snippet file.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|internal|
|» visibility|public|
|» » action|create|
|» » action|update|
|» » action|delete|
|» » action|move|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-software-composition-analysis">Software composition analysis</h1>

Use this API to upload the SBOM produced by a CI/CD job, download the resulting scan, and reuse a
scan that already exists for the same SBOM.

## Authorize SBOM file upload

<a id="opIdpostApiV4JobsIdSbomScansAuthorize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/jobs/0/sbom_scans/authorize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "filesize": 0
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/jobs/{id}/sbom_scans/authorize`

Authorizes uploading an SBOM file to be scanned for a specified job.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filesize": 0
}
```

<h3 id="authorize-sbom-file-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the job.|
|body|body|[postApiV4JobsIdSbomScansAuthorizeRequest](#schemapostapiv4jobsidsbomscansauthorizerequest)|false|none|
|» filesize|body|integer \| null|false|Size of the artifact file.|

<h3 id="authorize-sbom-file-upload-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|SBOM Upload allowed|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|
|413|Payload Too Large|File too large|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Upload an SBOM file

<a id="opIdpostApiV4JobsIdSbomScans"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/jobs/0/sbom_scans \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'sbom_digest=string'
```

`POST /api/v4/jobs/{id}/sbom_scans`

Uploads an SBOM file to be scanned for a specified job.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
sbom_digest: string
```

<h3 id="upload-an-sbom-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the job.|
|body|body|[postApiV4JobsIdSbomScansRequest](#schemapostapiv4jobsidsbomscansrequest)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary) \| null|true|The sbom file to upload|
|» sbom_digest|body|string \| null|false|Digest corresponding to uploaded SBOM|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "download_url": "string",
  "throttled": true,
  "project_throttling_resets_in": 0,
  "advisory_db_state": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="upload-an-sbom-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|

|400|Bad Request|Bad request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|
|413|Payload Too Large|File too large|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Reuse SBOM scan results

<a id="opIdpostApiV4JobsIdSbomScansSbomDigest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/jobs/0/sbom_scans/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
```

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-storage-moves">Storage moves</h1>

Use this API to schedule and track [repository storage moves](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/operations/moving_repositories/)
for groups, projects, and snippets. Project moves cover wiki and design repositories, and group
moves cover [group wikis](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/wiki/group/). Moving repositories
can help you [migrate to Gitaly Cluster (Praefect)](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/gitaly/praefect/#migrate-to-gitaly-cluster-praefect).

To ensure data integrity, GitLab places the group, project, or snippet in a temporary read-only
state for the duration of the move. During this time, users receive this message if they try to
push new commits:

```plaintext
The repository is temporarily read-only. Please try again later.
```

This API requires you to [authenticate yourself](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/) as an administrator.

## States

As GitLab processes a storage move, it transitions through different states. Values of `state` are:

- `initial`: The record has been created, but the background job has not yet been scheduled.
- `scheduled`: The background job has been scheduled.
- `started`: The repositories are being copied to the destination storage.
- `replicated`: The repositories have been moved.
- `failed`: The repositories failed to copy, or the checksums did not match.
- `finished`: The repositories have been moved, and the repositories on the source storage have been deleted.
- `cleanup failed`: The repositories have been moved, but the repositories on the source storage could not be deleted.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/group_repository_storage_moves/">External documentation</a>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-submodules">Submodules</h1>

Use this API to update [Git submodules](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Submodules).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/repository_submodules/">External documentation</a>

## Update a submodule reference

<a id="opIdputApiV4ProjectsIdRepositorySubmodulesSubmodule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/gitlab-org%2Fgitlab/repository/submodules/gitlab-org%2Fgitlab-shell \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "commit_sha": "ed899a2f4b50b4370feeea94676502b42383c746",
    "branch": "main",
    "commit_message": "Commit message"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/submodules/{submodule}`

Updates a reference for a specified submodule.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "commit_sha": "ed899a2f4b50b4370feeea94676502b42383c746",
  "branch": "main",
  "commit_message": "Commit message"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-submodule-reference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|submodule|path|string|true|URL-encoded full path to the submodule, for example `lib%2Fclass%2Erb`.|
|body|body|[putApiV4ProjectsIdRepositorySubmodulesSubmoduleRequest](#schemaputapiv4projectsidrepositorysubmodulessubmodulerequest)|true|none|
|» commit_sha|body|string \| null|true|Full commit SHA to update the submodule to.|
|» branch|body|string \| null|true|Name of the branch to commit into.|
|» commit_message|body|string \| null|false|Commit message. If omitted, a default message is used.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "2695effb5807a22ff3d138d593fd856244e155e7",
  "short_id": "2695effb",
  "created_at": "2017-07-26T11:08:53.000+02:00",
  "parent_ids": [
    "2a4b78934375d7f53875269ffd4f45fd83a84ebe"
  ],
  "title": "Initial commit",
  "message": "Initial commit",
  "author_name": "John Smith",
  "author_email": "john@example.com",
  "authored_date": "2012-05-28T04:42:42-07:00",
  "committer_name": "Jack Smith",
  "committer_email": "jack@example.com",
  "committed_date": "2012-05-28T04:42:42-07:00",
  "trailers": {
    "Merged-By": "Jane Doe janedoe@gitlab.com"
  },
  "extended_trailers": {
    "Signed-off-by": [
      "John Doe <johndoe@gitlab.com>",
      "Jane Doe <janedoe@gitlab.com>"
    ]
  },
  "web_url": "https://gitlab.example.com/janedoe/gitlab-foss/-/commit/ed899a2f4b50b4370feeea94676502b42383c746",
  "stats": {
    "additions": 1,
    "deletions": 0,
    "total": 1
  },
  "status": "success",
  "project_id": 1,
  "last_pipeline": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-submodule-reference-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesCommitDetail](#schemaapientitiescommitdetail)|
|400|Bad Request|The repository is empty|None|
|401|Unauthorized|401 Unauthorized|None|
|404|Not Found|404 Project Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-suggestions">Suggestions</h1>

Use this API to manage [code suggestions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/reviews/suggestions/).

Suggestions provide a way to propose specific changes that can be directly applied to the code.
You can programmatically create and apply code suggestions in merge request discussions with
this API. Every API call to suggestions must be authenticated.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/suggestions/">External documentation</a>

## Apply a suggestion to a merge request

<a id="opIdputApiV4SuggestionsIdApply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/suggestions/0/apply \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "commit_message": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/suggestions/{id}/apply`

Applies a suggested patch in a merge request. You must have the Developer, Maintainer, or Owner role.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "commit_message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-suggestion-to-a-merge-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|ID of the suggestion.|
|body|body|[putApiV4SuggestionsIdApplyRequest](#schemaputapiv4suggestionsidapplyrequest)|false|none|
|» commit_message|body|string \| null|false|Custom commit message to use instead of the default generated message or the project's default message.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "from_line": 1,
  "to_line": 1,
  "appliable": true,
  "applied": false,
  "from_content": "Original content\n",
  "to_content": "New content\n"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-suggestion-to-a-merge-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesSuggestion](#schemaapientitiessuggestion)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Apply multiple suggestions to a merge request

<a id="opIdputApiV4SuggestionsBatchApply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/suggestions/batch_apply \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ids": [
      0
    ],
    "commit_message": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v4/suggestions/batch_apply`

Applies multiple suggested patches in a merge request. You must have the Developer, Maintainer, or Owner role.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ids": [
    0
  ],
  "commit_message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-multiple-suggestions-to-a-merge-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[putApiV4SuggestionsBatchApplyRequest](#schemaputapiv4suggestionsbatchapplyrequest)|true|none|
|» ids|body|[integer]|true|IDs of suggestions to apply.|
|» commit_message|body|string \| null|false|Custom commit message to use instead of the default generated message or the project's default message.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "from_line": 1,
  "to_line": 1,
  "appliable": true,
  "applied": false,
  "from_content": "Original content\n",
  "to_content": "New content\n"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[APIEntitiesSuggestion](#schemaapientitiessuggestion)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|

</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-tags">Tags</h1>

Use this API to manage [Git tags](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/tags/). This API also returns X.509
signature information from signed tags.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/tags/">External documentation</a>

## List all project repository tags

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/repository/tags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/tags`

Lists all repository tags from a project, sorted by update date and time in descending order.

<h3 id="list-all-project-repository-tags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort results in ascending or descending order.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Sort results by the specified field. Sorting by version uses the semantic version number.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Return only tags matching the search criteria. Use `^term` to find tags that begin with `term`, and `term$` to find tags that end with `term`. No other regular expressions are supported.|
|page_token|query|string \| null|false|Name of the tag to start the pagination from. Used for keyset pagination.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items to list per page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|asc|
|sort|desc|
|order_by|name|
|order_by|updated|
|order_by|version|

## Create a tag

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/repository/tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tag_name": "v.1.0.0",
    "ref": "2695effb5807a22ff3d138d593fd856244e155e7",
    "message": "Release 1.0.0"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/repository/tags`

Creates a tag in the repository that points to a specified reference.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tag_name": "v.1.0.0",
  "ref": "2695effb5807a22ff3d138d593fd856244e155e7",
  "message": "Release 1.0.0"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-tag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdRepositoryTagsRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidrepositorytagsrequest)|true|none|
|» tag_name|body|string \| null|true|Name of the tag.|
|» ref|body|string \| null|true|Commit SHA or name of the branch or tag to create the tag from.|
|» message|body|string \| null|false|Message for the annotated tag. If specified, creates an annotated tag.|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-templates">Templates</h1>

Use this API to retrieve the file templates available to an entire instance:

- [Dockerfile templates](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-foss/-/tree/master/vendor/Dockerfile)
- [`.gitignore` templates](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore)
- [CI/CD configuration templates](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/lib/gitlab/ci/templates)
- [Open source license templates](https://choosealicense.com/)

Custom CI/CD templates are not available from these endpoints. For templates specific to a project,
use the [project templates API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/project_templates/).

Users with the Guest role can't access these templates. For more information, see
[project and group visibility](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/public_access/).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/templates/dockerfiles/">External documentation</a>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-terraform">Terraform</h1>

Use this API to interact with the [Terraform CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/terraform_module_registry/).

> [!warning]
> This API is used by the [Terraform CLI](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform)
> and is generally not meant for manual consumption. Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/packages/terraform-modules/">External documentation</a>

## Retrieve a Terraform state version

<a id="opIdgetApiV4ProjectsIdTerraformStateNameVersionsSerial"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/terraform/state/string/versions/0 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/terraform/state/{name}/versions/{serial}`

Retrieves a specified Terraform state version.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-terraform-state-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the Terraform state.|
|serial|path|integer|true|Version number of the Terraform state.|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-terraform-state-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

## Create or update a Terraform state

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/terraform/state/string \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

|» file|body|string(binary) \| null|true|The package file to be published (generated by Multipart middleware)|

## Lock a Terraform state

<a id="opIdpostApiV4ProjectsIdTerraformStateNameLock"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/projects/string/terraform/state/string/lock \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ID": "string",
    "Operation": "string",
    "Info": "string",
    "Who": "string",
    "Version": "string",
    "Created": "string",
    "Path": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/terraform/state/{name}/lock`

Locks a Terraform state for a specified project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ID": "string",
  "Operation": "string",
  "Info": "string",
  "Who": "string",
  "Version": "string",
  "Created": "string",
  "Path": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="lock-a-terraform-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string \| integer|true|ID or URL-encoded path of the project.|
|name|path|string|true|Name of the Terraform state.|
|body|body|[postApiV4ProjectsIdTerraformStateNameLockRequest](#schemapostapiv4projectsidterraformstatenamelockrequest)|true|none|
|» ID|body|string \| null|true|Terraform state lock ID.|
|» Operation|body|string \| null|true|Terraform operation.|
|» Info|body|string \| null|true|Terraform info|
|» Who|body|string \| null|true|Terraform state lock owner|
|» Version|body|string \| null|true|Terraform version|
|» Created|body|string \| null|true|Terraform state lock timestamp|
|» Path|body|string \| null|true|Terraform path|

<h3 id="lock-a-terraform-state-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

|404|Not Found|Not found|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failure|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-to-dos">To-dos</h1>

Use this API to list [to-do items](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/todos/), mark them as done, and
create a to-do item for an issue or a merge request.

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-token-exchange">Token exchange</h1>

Use this API to exchange a token for a short-lived JWT that is scoped to a single GitLab service
audience.

## Issue a short-lived JWT for a single modular-service audience

<a id="opIdpostApiV4TokenExchange"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/token_exchange \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "audience": "gitlab-artifact-registry",
    "expires_in": 300
  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/token_exchange`

Issues a short-lived RS256 JWT scoped to one modular-service audience (such as the Artifact Registry). Claims include the requesting user id (sub), organization id, and deployment realm (saas / self-managed). Presented to the corresponding backend and verified against the instance JWKS.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audience": "gitlab-artifact-registry",
  "expires_in": 300
}
```

<h3 id="issue-a-short-lived-jwt-for-a-single-modular-service-audience-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[postApiV4TokenExchangeRequest](#schemapostapiv4tokenexchangerequest)|true|none|
|» audience|body|string|true|Target service audience.|
|» expires_in|body|integer|false|Requested token lifetime in seconds. The granted lifetime may be shorter than requested depending on the authentication method used to call this endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» audience|gitlab-artifact-registry|

<h3 id="issue-a-short-lived-jwt-for-a-single-modular-service-audience-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
http, oauth2, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-unleash">Unleash</h1>

endpoints are used by an Unleash client and are not meant for manual consumption.

## Report Unleash client metrics

<a id="opIdpostApiV4FeatureFlagsUnleashProjectIdClientMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/feature_flags/unleash/string/client/metrics \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
```

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-usage-data">Usage data</h1>

GitLab collects, including its non-SQL metrics and the queries behind it.

## Track an internal GitLab event

<a id="opIdpostApiV4UsageDataTrackEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://gitlab.com/api/v4/api/v4/usage_data/track_event \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "event": "i_quickactions_page",

      "value": 1
    },

  }'
```

`POST /api/v4/usage_data/track_event`

Tracks a GitLab internal event. This action increments Service Ping counters in Redis and is optionally sent to Snowplow. Introduced in GitLab 16.2.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event": "i_quickactions_page",
  "namespace_id": 1234,
  "project_id": 1234,
  "project_path": "namespace/project",
  "additional_properties": {
    "label": "login_button",
    "value": 1
  },
  "send_to_snowplow": true
}
```

<h3 id="track-an-internal-gitlab-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[postApiV4UsageDataTrackEventRequest](#schemapostapiv4usagedatatrackeventrequest)|true|none|
|» event|body|string \| null|true|Name of the event to track.|
|» namespace_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the namespace associated with the event.|
|» project_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the project. Mutually exclusive with `project_path`.|
|» project_path|body|string \| null|false|Path of the project. Used to find `project_id` when it is not provided. Mutually exclusive with `project_id`.|
|» additional_properties|body|object \| null|false|Additional properties to be tracked.|
|» send_to_snowplow|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, sends the tracked event to Snowplow.|

|404|Not Found|Not found|None|

<h1 id="gitlab-rest-api-users">Users</h1>

Use this API to interact with user accounts on GitLab. These endpoints can help manage
[your account](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/), manage
[accounts for other users](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/administer_users/),
[moderate user accounts](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/moderate_users/),
[perform follower actions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/#follow-users), and
[interact with email addresses for user accounts](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/).

<a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/api/users/">External documentation</a>
